root_cause.text: The trigger_data_free() function deferred freeing of event_trigger_data objects to a cleanup kthread during boot, but failed to drain the accumulated deferred-free list if kthread creation never succeeded, causing memory leaks and NULL pointer dereferences when subsequent frees attempted to use the non-existent kthread.
root_cause.evidence: The patch shows that before the fix, when `trigger_kthread` was NULL after kthread creation failed, the code would either queue items to `trigger_data_free_list` or perform slow synchronous frees, but never drained the queued list. The fix adds `trigger_data_free_queued_locked()` to synchronously drain the entire `trigger_data_free_list` when kthread creation fails, and adds a `late_initcall(trigger_data_free_init)` to drain any remaining queued entries at late init time. The CVE description confirms this: "boot-deferred nodes can accumulate on trigger_data_free_list, later frees fall back to synchronously freeing only the current object, and the older queued entries are leaked forever."

intent_record.intent_summary: Extract common kthread creation and queued data freeing logic into reusable helper functions with proper locking assertions to reduce code duplication and improve maintainability.
intent_record.what: Added two new static helper functions: trigger_create_kthread_locked() which creates a kthread for trigger_data_free if one doesn't exist, and trigger_data_free_queued_locked() which processes and frees queued trigger_data elements from the free list. Both functions include lockdep_assert_held() to verify mutex ownership.
intent_record.how: These functions extract and encapsulate logic that was previously inline or duplicated elsewhere in the code. trigger_create_kthread_locked() safely initializes the trigger_kthread with error checking, while trigger_data_free_queued_locked() atomically drains the free list, synchronizes unregistration, and frees all queued data structures. Both enforce that the caller holds trigger_data_kthread_mutex, preventing race conditions.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix boot-time trigger registration failures by deferring kthread creation to late init and queuing frees until the kthread is ready.
intent_record.what: Refactored trigger_data_free() to defer kthread creation until late boot, extracted kthread creation logic into trigger_create_kthread_locked() helper, added boot-time check to queue frees during SYSTEM_BOOTING, added trigger_data_free_init() late_initcall to drain queued frees, and removed inline kthread creation code from the main free path.
intent_record.how: The change defers kthread initialization to late boot phase, allowing trigger data to be safely queued for deferred freeing during early boot when kthread creation may fail. During SYSTEM_BOOTING, frees are added to a list instead of attempting immediate kthread creation. A new late_initcall handler processes any queued items once the kthread is successfully created. This prevents boot-time failures from kthread creation attempts and ensures proper cleanup semantics across boot phases.

relevance_review.reason: The group focuses on extracting common logic into helper functions for code reuse and maintainability. While it may involve kthread creation and data freeing, the core vulnerability issue is about handling the failure case when kthread creation never succeeds and draining the deferred-free list. Refactoring for code reuse does not directly address the missing cleanup logic for failed kthread initialization.

This group directly addresses the root cause by deferring kthread creation to late init and ensuring frees are queued only when the kthread is ready. This prevents the scenario where deferred-free operations accumulate without a valid kthread to process them, which was the core issue causing memory leaks and NULL pointer dereferences.

The event trigger data requires a full tracepoint_sy
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 61d445af0a7c70018111919e47beaaee15653f2f
Author: Steven Rostedt <rostedt@goodmis.org>
Date:   Tue Nov 25 16:40:06 2025 -0500

    tracing: Add bulk garbage collection of freeing event_trigger_data
    
    The event trigger data requires a full tracepoint_synchronize_unregister()
    call before freeing. That call can take 100s of milliseconds to complete.
    In order to allow for bulk freeing of the trigger data, it can not call
    the tracepoint_synchronize_unregister() for every indi
bic_trace_step.reason: This commit introduces the bulk garbage collection mechanism for event_trigger_data freeing. The code shows proper handling of the kthread creation failure case: (1) Lines 48-49 check if trigger_kthread is NULL and attempt creation within a mutex-protected critical section; (2) Lines 50-52 perform a double-check pattern after acquiring the mutex; (3) Lines 53-57 create the kthread with IS_ERR() validation; (4) Critically, lines 59-65 handle the case where trigger_kthread remains NULL (kthread creation failed) by falling back to the slow synchronous path: calling tracepoint_synchronize_unregister() directly and freeing immediately with kfree(data), then returning early; (5) Only if trigger_kthread was successfully created does the code defer the free to the llist (lines 67-68). This prevents the vulnerability described in the root cause - if kthread creation fails, the code does NOT attempt to use a non-existent kthread, and does NOT leak memory by deferring to a cleanup list that will never be processed. The fallback mechanism ensures correct behavior even when kthread creation fails.
